beats.label: S1 · Crash and the 16-year signal
beats.text: Oceanic 815 breaks up over an uncharted island. Survivors regroup on the beach and pick up a French distress loop that has been repeating for sixteen years.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the premise and the first sign that the island is not what it seems.

beats.label: S1 · Locke walks
beats.text: Paraplegic before the flight, Locke wakes able to walk. He faces the island's creature and calls it beautiful, forming a faith Jack will spend the season resisting.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Seeds the Jack/Locke science-vs-faith split that structures every later season.

beats.label: S1 · Ethan and the Others
beats.text: Danielle Rousseau, source of the signal, warns of hostile 'Others.' Ethan Rom is exposed as an intruder on the manifest, abducts Claire, and is killed before he can explain.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First proof the island is inhabited by an organised, hostile group — the antagonists for years to come.

beats.label: S1 · The hatch and Boone
beats.text: Chasing visions, Locke finds a sealed hatch buried in the jungle. His refusal to abandon it gets Boone killed on a drug-runner's plane, and Shannon holds Locke responsible.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the hatch — the season's engine — and the first death caused by Locke's obsession.

beats.label: S1 · Aaron and the boy
beats.text: Claire delivers a son, Aaron. Rousseau steals him to trade for her lost daughter, revealing the Others are hunting 'the boy'; the survivors get Aaron back.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Aaron's existence and the Others' interest in a child are both live threads going into S2.

beats.label: S1 · The raft and Walt
beats.text: Michael, Jin, Sawyer and Walt sail out on a raft. Strangers intercept them at sea, shoot Sawyer, blow up the raft and take Walt as 'the boy' they came for.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Walt's abduction is the fuse that drives Michael's entire arc in S2.

beats.label: S1 · The hatch, blown open
beats.text: Rousseau warns the Others are coming. Jack, Locke and Kate blast the hatch open with Black Rock dynamite while Hurley freezes at the numbers etched into its rim.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The literal question S2 opens with — what is inside — and Hurley's numbers first colliding with the island itself.

cliffhanger.text: The hatch stands open with a light burning at the bottom. Walt is somewhere at sea in the hands of strangers, Sawyer is bleeding out on a pontoon, and Rousseau's warning about the Others has just come true.
questions: What is down inside the hatch, and why are Hurley's numbers on it?
Who took Walt, and what is 'the boy' they were hunting?
Who are the Others, and what do they want with the survivors?

characters.name: Jack Shephard
characters.line: Surgeon and reluctant leader. Man of science, split from Locke over the hatch, still haunted by finding his father dead in Sydney.

characters.name: John Locke
characters.line: Was paraplegic before the crash and walks on the island. Believes the crash was destiny; the group's hunter and its man of faith.

characters.name: Kate Austen
characters.line: Federal fugitive posing as a survivor, caught between Jack and Sawyer; the marshal transporting her lingered wounded from the crash until Jack was forced to kill him.

characters.name: James 'Sawyer' Ford
characters.line: Con-man with the group's stash of scavenged goods; met Jack's dying father in a Sydney bar without knowing who he was.

characters.name: Hurley Reyes
characters.line: Cursed lottery winner who compiled the survivors' manifest and just recognised his numbers on the hatch.

characters.name: Sayid Jarrah
characters.line: Former Iraqi Republican Guard. Repaired the transceiver, made first contact with Rousseau, and is beginning something with Shannon.

characters.name: Charlie Pace
characters.line: Rock bassist who kicked heroin on the island. Devoted to Claire and Aaron since rescuing them from Ethan.

characters.name: Claire Littleton
characters.line: Australian single mother to newborn Aaron; briefly abducted by the impostor Ethan and can't remember it.

characters.name: Michael Dawson
characters.line: Estranged father who barely knew his ten-year-old son Walt. Just lost him again to strangers at sea.

characters.name: Sun-Hwa Kwon
characters.line: Wife of Jin; secretly speaks English. Poisoned Jin's water to keep him from leaving on the raft — and it worked, badly.

characters.name: Jin-Soo Kwon
characters.line: Sun's husband, once her father's enforcer. Was on the raft when it was destroyed and dragged into the sea.

beats.label: S2 · The Swan and the button
beats.text: The hatch is a DHARMA bunker called the Swan. Its lone inhabitant Desmond Hume must enter numbers every 108 minutes to prevent catastrophe; Locke takes the duty as gospel.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Desmond and the ritual whose eventual failure defines the finale.

beats.label: S2 · The Tailies arrive
beats.text: Michael, Jin and Sawyer wash up among the tail-section survivors led by ex-cop Ana Lucia, who mistakes Shannon for an Other and shoots her; the two groups merge on the beach.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Doubles the cast, brings Eko and Libby into play, and kills off Shannon in the transition.

beats.label: S2 · Michael runs for Walt
beats.text: A message from Walt reaches the Swan's computer. Michael steals a bag of guns and disappears into the jungle to get his son back.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Michael's obsession pointed at Walt is the mechanism that will get others killed in the finale.

beats.label: S2 · 'Henry Gale'
beats.text: Rousseau captures a man calling himself Henry Gale. Sayid's interrogations and the real Henry Gale's corpse in the jungle prove he is an Other, and he is locked in the armory.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First real Other in captivity, and the manipulator who will drive the finale from inside a cell.

beats.label: S2 · Michael's betrayal
beats.text: The Others promise Michael his son back if he frees Henry and hands over Jack, Kate, Sawyer and Hurley. He shoots Ana Lucia and Libby to spring Henry from the armory.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns Michael into the season's true traitor and sets up the ambush at the finale.

beats.label: S2 · Locke breaks the button
beats.text: Shaken by an orientation film calling the Swan a psychological experiment, Locke wrestles Eko for the terminal and blocks the numbers as the timer runs out.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's central act of faith-collapse — the button is not pushed, on purpose.

beats.label: S2 · Fail-safe and the ambush
beats.text: Desmond turns a fail-safe key, imploding the Swan in a violet flash. The Others ambush the trade and take Jack, Kate, Sawyer and Hurley; Michael sails away with Walt.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the season with four of the leads captured and the Swan gone — the exact state S3 opens in.

cliffhanger.text: The Swan has imploded in a violet burst that lit up the sky. Jack, Kate, Sawyer and Hurley are prisoners of the Others. Michael and Walt are motoring away to freedom, alone, having gotten there by murder.
questions: Who are the Others and what do they want with these four?
What did Desmond's fail-safe actually do to the island?
Will Michael and Walt make it home, and what will they do with what they know?

characters.name: Jack Shephard
characters.line: Now a captive of the Others alongside Kate, Sawyer and Hurley after walking into the ambush.

characters.name: Kate Austen
characters.line: Captive of the Others; deepened her push-pull with both Jack and Sawyer over the season.

characters.name: James 'Sawyer' Ford
characters.line: Captive of the Others; shot and slowly nursed back to health by the Tailies before the ambush.

characters.name: Hurley Reyes
characters.line: Captive of the Others; grew closer to Libby before Michael shot her.

characters.name: John Locke
characters.line: His faith in the button broken, he let the Swan implode. On the beach, alive.

characters.name: Sayid Jarrah
characters.line: On the beach with the main group; the one who unmasked 'Henry Gale' as an Other.

characters.name: Charlie Pace
characters.line: Estranged from Claire after the statue stash and baptism confrontation; lapsed briefly back toward heroin.

characters.name: Claire Littleton
characters.line: Recovered her lost memories of being taken to the Others' medical station; wary of Charlie.

characters.name: Sun-Hwa Kwon
characters.line: Unexpectedly pregnant, reconciled with Jin, still on the beach.

characters.name: Jin-Soo Kwon
characters.line: Reconciled with Sun and now speaking a little English; back on the beach after the raft.

characters.name: Michael Dawson
characters.line: Sailed away with Walt after murdering Ana Lucia and Libby to break 'Henry' out of the armory.

characters.name: Desmond Hume
characters.line: Scot who spent three years pushing the button. Turned the fail-safe key and vanished into the implosion.

characters.name: 'Henry Gale'
characters.line: The captured Other who manipulated the survivors from a cell all season and walked out of the Swan a free man.

beats.label: S3 · Cages on Hydra
beats.text: Jack, Kate and Sawyer wake caged on a second, smaller island near the Others' Hydra station. Fertility doctor Juliet Burke works Jack for a spinal surgery on their leader, Ben.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the Others' world, introduces Juliet, and puts Ben's body clock on Jack's operating table.

beats.label: S3 · Juliet flips
beats.text: Jack cuts Ben during surgery to force Kate and Sawyer's release; they flee. Juliet returns with them to the beach as Ben's mole, then quietly switches sides.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Places Juliet inside the main camp — a new pillar of the ensemble going forward.

beats.label: S3 · Locke joins the Others
beats.text: Locke, spun by Ben, blows up the Others' submarine — their only way home — and convinces Sawyer to strangle his father Anthony Cooper as his rite of passage.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Commits Locke to the Others and, incidentally, to Ben's plan to keep the island unreachable.

beats.label: S3 · Naomi and the freighter
beats.text: A woman named Naomi Dorrit parachutes onto the island, claiming to have been sent by Penny Widmore. Ben insists she is lying and will bring people who mean to kill everyone.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the freighter that drives all of S4.

beats.label: S3 · Jacob's cabin
beats.text: Ben takes Locke to a cabin and pretends to consult a man named Jacob. An unseen voice pleads 'help me'; Ben then shoots Locke and leaves him for dead in a mass grave.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First mention of Jacob, and Ben's answer to Locke gaining status among the Others.

beats.label: S3 · Charlie in the Looking Glass
beats.text: Desmond sees Charlie's death in visions. Charlie unjams the island's signal from an underwater station, learns from Penny that Naomi's boat isn't hers, and drowns writing the warning.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kills Charlie and establishes that the freighter is not what it claims — the season's whole thesis.

beats.label: S3 · 'We have to go back'
beats.text: Jack radios the freighter over Locke's warning and Charlie's message. Later, off the island, a broken Jack tells Kate they were wrong to leave — 'we have to go back.'
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reveals the show now runs both directions in time, and that some of them get off. The engine for S4.

cliffhanger.text: Jack has called the freighter over Charlie's dying warning that it isn't Penny's. And in a flash the show has just admitted is the future, off the island, a bearded and broken Jack tells Kate they need to go back.
questions: Who is really on Naomi's freighter, and what do they want with the island?
Which survivors make it off, and why does Jack come to regret it so completely?
What was the loophole Ben was so desperate to prevent — was he telling the truth?

characters.name: Jack Shephard
characters.line: Just radioed the freighter over Locke and Ben's warnings; the survivors' leader again.

characters.name: Kate Austen
characters.line: Chose Sawyer over Jack on the second island; back on the beach.

characters.name: James 'Sawyer' Ford
characters.line: Killed the Other Tom during the beach raid; back with the survivors after the escape from the cages.

characters.name: Hurley Reyes
characters.line: Drove a rescued DHARMA van into the beach raid and saved Sayid's ambushed team.

characters.name: Sayid Jarrah
characters.line: On the beach; led the team that killed most of the Others in the raid.

characters.name: John Locke
characters.line: Shot by Ben in the DHARMA grave, survived, and just stabbed Naomi to try and stop the freighter call.

characters.name: Juliet Burke
characters.line: Ex-Others fertility doctor turned defector; permitted to live on the beach.

characters.name: Ben Linus
characters.line: Captured leader of the Others, beaten by Jack, and still claiming the freighter will kill them all.

characters.name: Desmond Hume
characters.line: Survived the Swan implosion with visions of the future; the one who saw Charlie's death coming.

characters.name: Sun-Hwa Kwon
characters.line: Pregnant; the Others' station confirmed the baby is Jin's.

characters.name: Jin-Soo Kwon
characters.line: Expectant father; on the beach with Sun.

characters.name: Claire Littleton
characters.line: Back with Charlie's memory as of the season's last act — she has just been widowed by his mission.

characters.name: Naomi Dorrit
characters.line: The parachutist claiming to represent Penny; stabbed by Locke, dead or dying just after making the call.

beats.label: S4 · The freighter people
beats.text: Naomi's team arrives: physicist Daniel Faraday, medium Miles Straume, anthropologist Charlotte Lewis, pilot Frank Lapidus. They are not a rescue party — they are hunting Ben.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces four characters who will each carry major threads for the rest of the show.

beats.label: S4 · The camp splits
beats.text: Locke's faction takes Ben and Claire with baby Aaron to the Barracks; Jack's stays on the beach to trust the freighter, splitting the survivors along faith and science again.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Redraws the map of who is with whom for the whole season.

beats.label: S4 · Time skew, and Penny
beats.text: Daniel's tests show island time runs out of sync with the outside world. Desmond's consciousness slips between years, and Penny Widmore, his 'constant,' anchors him back.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes that the island is temporally displaced and gives Desmond his lifeline going forward.

beats.label: S4 · Ben's spy is Michael
beats.text: Ben's man on the freighter turns out to be Michael, working under an alias. He warns the survivors its owner, Charles Widmore, means to kill everyone once he has Ben.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the ultimate enemy — Widmore — and returns Michael as a variable.

beats.label: S4 · Keamy and Alex
beats.text: Widmore's mercenary Martin Keamy lands and murders Ben's daughter Alex to force him out. Ben summons the smoke monster on Keamy's team and vows to kill Penny in revenge.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns Ben from captor to grief-driven, and defines his agenda past this season.

beats.label: S4 · Move the island
beats.text: Ben kills Keamy, whose dead-man's switch destroys the freighter with Michael and Jin aboard. Then Ben turns a frozen wheel under the Orchid and the island itself vanishes from the sea.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The finale action that separates everyone left behind from everyone rescued.

beats.label: S4 · The Oceanic Six
beats.text: Six survivors reach shore and lie about the rest. Years later, a broken Jack meets Ben at Locke's coffin — the Oceanic Six must return, with Locke's body.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the group, establishes the lie, and sets the how-do-they-get-back problem for S5.

cliffhanger.text: The island is gone. The Oceanic Six have been living a public lie for years; the rest of the survivors have been abandoned somewhere in time. Jack has finally cracked, standing over Locke's coffin as Ben tells him everyone left has to come back — and take the body with them.
questions: What happened on the island to the people the Six left behind when Ben moved it?
How can they possibly return to an island that has vanished from the ocean?
What went so wrong off-island that even Locke's coffin has to be dragged back?

characters.name: Jack Shephard
characters.line: Oceanic Six. Bearded, drinking, obsessed with returning; the one Ben is now working on.

characters.name: Kate Austen
characters.line: Oceanic Six. Free thanks to the cover story; raising Aaron off-island as her own son.

characters.name: Hurley Reyes
characters.line: Oceanic Six. Voluntarily committed himself to Santa Rosa, haunted by visions of dead friends.

characters.name: Sayid Jarrah
characters.line: Oceanic Six. Married Nadia briefly; recruited by Ben as his off-island assassin against Widmore's people.

characters.name: Sun-Hwa Kwon
characters.line: Oceanic Six. Gave birth to Ji Yeon believing Jin died on the freighter.

characters.name: Aaron
characters.line: Toddler being raised by Kate. Not actually her son; nobody outside the Six knows.

characters.name: Ben Linus
characters.line: Off-island in exile, orchestrating the Six's return; his daughter Alex was killed for his refusal to surrender.

characters.name: John Locke
characters.line: Dead off-island in a coffin. The last person Jack expected to be trying to bring back.

characters.name: James 'Sawyer' Ford
characters.line: Left behind on the island. Jumped out of the escape helicopter to spare the weight for Kate.

characters.name: Juliet Burke
characters.line: Left behind on the island with the beach camp; her side chosen.

characters.name: Desmond Hume
characters.line: Off-island on Penny's boat, reunited with her at last after slipping through time.

characters.name: Charles Widmore
characters.line: The billionaire who owned the freighter; wants the island and now wants Ben dead. Penny's father.

characters.name: Daniel Faraday
characters.line: Physicist who diagnosed the time skew. Was on a raft to the freighter with Sun and others when the island moved.

characters.name: Jin-Soo Kwon
characters.line: Presumed dead in the freighter explosion. Sun believes she is a widow.

beats.label: S5 · Time flashes
beats.text: Ben's turning the wheel triggers time flashes; those left behind — Sawyer, Juliet, Locke, Faraday, Miles, Charlotte — jerk through the island's past and future without warning.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's mechanic. Also strands Sawyer and Juliet in the era where DHARMA is still alive.

beats.label: S5 · Locke fixes the wheel
beats.text: Christian's ghost tells Locke he must leave to bring the Six back. Locke resets the wheel, ending the flashes but leaving him off-island and the others stranded in 1974.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Divides the surviving cast in time and sends Locke out into the world alone.

beats.label: S5 · Sawyer's DHARMA years
beats.text: Trapped in 1974, Sawyer's group joins the DHARMA Initiative under aliases. By 1977 he is head of security, lives with Juliet, and has quietly waited three years for a way home.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts the beach survivors inside DHARMA and pairs Sawyer and Juliet as a real couple.

beats.label: S5 · Locke as Jeremy Bentham
beats.text: Off-island, Locke fails to convince the Six to return. Alone and beaten, he dies — the death Richard warned was necessary to bring them back with his body.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains the coffin and Ben's methods; sets the mechanism for the reunion flight.

beats.label: S5 · Ajira 316
beats.text: Guided by Eloise Hawking, the Six and Ben board Ajira 316 with Locke's coffin. Some flash back into DHARMA's 1977; Sun and Ben arrive on the island in 2007 with Locke's body.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reunites the cast across two eras, so both timelines can run in parallel.

beats.label: S5 · Jughead
beats.text: In 1977, convinced by the dying Faraday, Jack drops a hydrogen bomb into the drilling shaft that will one day be the Swan, hoping to erase Flight 815's crash. Juliet strikes the core and everything whites out.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The 1977 climax that resolves the flashes and probably kills Juliet.

beats.label: S5 · The loophole
beats.text: 'Locke' walks out of the jungle alive in 2007 and leads Ben to meet Jacob inside a giant statue. Ben stabs Jacob dead — then the real Locke's body is unloaded from Ajira 316 on the beach.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reveals the man leading the Others is not Locke, and that Jacob — barely mentioned till now — was real and is dead.

cliffhanger.text: Jacob is dead, stabbed by Ben on the orders of a man wearing John Locke's face — while Locke's actual corpse sits in a crate on the beach. In 1977, Juliet has just struck the Jughead's core, and the screen has gone white.
questions: Did Juliet's strike reset the timeline, or did it kill her and her friends for nothing?
If the thing wearing Locke's face isn't Locke, what is it and what did it want with Jacob dead?
Who is Jacob, and what was he protecting the island from?

characters.name: Jack Shephard
characters.line: In 1977 with DHARMA; just dropped the Jughead trying to erase the crash.

characters.name: Kate Austen
characters.line: In 1977 with Jack; came back to the island reluctantly and opposed the bomb plan.

characters.name: Hurley Reyes
characters.line: In 1977; brought the Six back on Ajira 316 at Jacob's urging.

characters.name: Sayid Jarrah
characters.line: In 1977; shot by Roger Linus and wounded in the DHARMA shootout.

characters.name: Jin-Soo Kwon
characters.line: Alive and in DHARMA in 1977; still separated from Sun by three decades.

characters.name: Sun-Hwa Kwon
characters.line: Arrived on the island in 2007 with Ben and Locke's body; hunting for Jin without knowing which era he's in.

characters.name: James 'Sawyer' Ford
characters.line: DHARMA security head 'LaFleur' in 1977; three years in love with Juliet.

characters.name: Juliet Burke
characters.line: In 1977 with Sawyer; struck the Jughead's core with a rock as she fell into the shaft.

characters.name: Ben Linus
characters.line: On the island in 2007; stabbed Jacob dead at the false Locke's command.

characters.name: John Locke
characters.line: His body has been on the beach the whole season, killed off-island and shipped back on Ajira 316.

characters.name: The Man in Black
characters.line: The being who has taken John Locke's form. Jacob's ancient enemy, who just found his 'loophole' to have Jacob killed.

characters.name: Richard Alpert
characters.line: Ageless advisor to the Others, who now understands that the man he has been following is not Locke.

beats.label: S6 · Two outcomes
beats.text: The Jughead's blast throws two outcomes on screen: on the island the 815ers wake alive in 2007, and in a 'sideways' timeline Flight 815 lands safely at LAX with everyone changed.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the season's dual structure — the sideways timeline whose meaning is the final answer.

beats.label: S6 · The temple and the 'infected'
beats.text: The Others revive a dying Sayid in the temple's healing spring. Their leader Dogen warns Jack the water was tainted — Sayid is now 'infected,' as Claire has been for three years.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the corruption that lets the monster claim two of the leads.

beats.label: S6 · The Man in Black's recruits
beats.text: The smoke monster in Locke's form recruits Sawyer, showing him a cave of names left by Jacob. Sayid and Claire join him; the temple is massacred when he walks in.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Splits the survivors between Jacob's replacement candidates and the monster's followers.

beats.label: S6 · Candidates
beats.text: Jack learns from Jacob that the survivors are candidates. One of them must replace him as the island's protector, or the Man in Black — the true smoke monster — escapes into the world.
beats.whyLoadBearing: States the season's job: pick a successor before the monster gets loose.

beats.label: S6 · The sub
beats.text: The Man in Black steers Sawyer's escape onto Widmore's sub and hides a bomb in Jack's pack. Sayid carries it away and dies; Sun and Jin drown together as the sub floods.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kills off Sayid, Sun and Jin in one act — the emotional cost of the season.

beats.label: S6 · Jack takes the mantle
beats.text: Jacob makes Jack the new protector. Ben kills Widmore. Desmond, immune to the light at the island's heart, is lowered into its shaft to be used to plug it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the final confrontation: Desmond as the weapon, Jack as the guardian.

beats.label: S6 · The end
beats.text: Jack duels the false Locke above the light. Kate kills the now-mortal Man in Black. Jack plugs the light and dies of his wounds; the sideways is revealed as an afterlife where they all reunite.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The finale itself: monster destroyed, Jack dies, sideways revealed.

cliffhanger.text: The island survived. Its protector died to save it. Everyone who mattered — the ones who lived, the ones who died on the sub, the ones who died decades apart — finally gathered in a place they built together to find each other again.
questions: Does the island endure under its new protector after Jack is gone?
Were the connections in the sideways ever real, or only what the dead needed to reconcile?
Was there ever a way through this story that didn't demand this much from these people?

characters.name: Jack Shephard
characters.line: Became the island's protector after Jacob, killed the monster's plan and died plugging the light.

characters.name: Kate Austen
characters.line: Shot the Man in Black once Desmond's meddling made him mortal; escaped on the Ajira plane.

characters.name: James 'Sawyer' Ford
characters.line: Escaped on the Ajira plane with Kate and Claire. Still blames himself for Juliet.

characters.name: Hurley Reyes
characters.line: Stayed on the island alongside Jack through the finale, one of the last candidates standing.

characters.name: Sayid Jarrah
characters.line: 'Infected' by the temple spring; died carrying the sub bomb away from the others.

characters.name: Sun-Hwa Kwon
characters.line: Drowned in the sub with Jin after finally reuniting with him.

characters.name: Jin-Soo Kwon
characters.line: Chose to drown with Sun rather than leave her trapped in the wreckage.

characters.name: Ben Linus
characters.line: Killed Widmore; stayed on the island with Hurley when everyone else left or died.

characters.name: John Locke
characters.line: The real Locke's body was buried after the monster was destroyed; only ever appeared alive this season in the sideways.

characters.name: The Man in Black
characters.line: The smoke monster in Locke's form. Made mortal by Desmond's uncorking the light, then shot dead.

characters.name: Desmond Hume
characters.line: Uniquely immune to electromagnetism; lowered into the light as the tool to make the monster killable.

characters.name: Claire Littleton
characters.line: Recovered from her three years feral in the jungle; escaped on the Ajira plane, going home to Aaron.
